Sample reports

What will your sponsor see?

Explore a before-and-after leadership assessment, the observations behind it and an example of how a multi-rater review could add another perspective.

Single-observer assessment

Leadership Growth Snapshot

Overall observer score

41% → 79%
On-time completion1 → 5 out of 5

The same observer rated one participant in April and July 2026. Adaptability remained the lowest competency at 67%.

Assessment details

One observer rated 45 behaviours across 15 competencies on 10 April and 31 July 2026. The score rose from 93 to 178 out of 225 points, a gain of 38 percentage points after rounding.

All 15 competencies improved. Adaptability and change readiness, at 67%, remained the clearest development need. These observations support a Level 3 discussion. Business impact requires separate measures.

Single-observer assessment

Observed Behavioural Change

Behaviours improved

44 of 45
Linking daily work to team goals3 → 3 out of 5

The one unchanged rating gives the manager a focus for the next check-in.

Assessment details

The observer recorded improvement on 44 behaviours. One stayed unchanged and none declined. Completing work on schedule rose from 1 to 5 on the five-point scale.

Linking daily work to team goals stayed at 3. This gives the manager a specific behaviour to revisit at the next check-in. This is the same participant and observer as the growth snapshot.

Programme design

From baseline to behaviour change.

A three-to-six-month journey across Self, People and Business, with manager observations on both sides of the programme.

How each module works

Use this indicative flow to plan the cohort with HR. Select a stage to explore its activities.

Establish the starting point

  • Brief participants on the context and pre-work.
  • Complete one profile: DiSC or Strengthscope®.
  • Ask the manager to evaluate current behaviour.
  • Debrief the participant individually.

Practise with a real case

  • Work through a workplace case in class.
  • Rehearse a response with peers in a simulation.
  • Use e-learning to reinforce the classroom work.
  • Review progress at a mid-module coaching check-in when coaching is selected.

Show what changed at work

  • Complete a workplace application assignment.
  • Discuss the experience in team or individual coaching when selected.
  • Present a final business case when a capstone is included.
  • Complete the post-assessment and review progress with the manager.
Pre-programme · Optional half dayOrientation schedule+

Six-month programme example · 260 minutes of activities

  1. 20 min
    Leadership team opening

    Connect the programme to organisational priorities.

  2. 30 min
    Programme roadmap

    Walk through the six-month journey, its requirements and assessment.

  3. 45 min
    Leadership reality check

    Discuss leadership challenges participants face in the organisation.

  4. 45 min
    Self-assessment

    Use DiSC via TalentValley to identify strengths and development gaps.

  5. 45 min
    Personal leadership challenge

    Select one workplace issue to address during the programme.

  6. 30 min
    Peer accountability groups

    Form groups of four or five for ongoing support.

  7. 30 min
    Commitment and manager alignment

    Agree goals, measures and the support needed from managers.

  8. 15 min
    Closing and immediate actions

    Confirm the first assignment and preparation for the first session.

Post-programme · Optional half dayGraduation schedule+

Six-month programme example · 250 minutes of activities

  1. 20 min
    Six-month journey review

    Revisit the objectives set at orientation.

  2. 45 min
    Leadership progress reflection

    Use the TalentValley report to compare starting and final development results.

  3. 90 min
    Workplace impact presentations

    Present the actions taken, results and lessons learned.

  4. 30 min
    Leadership panel feedback

    Senior leaders respond to the recommendations and progress presented.

  5. 30 min
    90-day action plan

    Commit to specific actions that will sustain development.

  6. 25 min
    Recognition and certificates

    Recognise participants’ achievements.

  7. 10 min
    Closing remarks from the leadership team

    Confirm expectations for the period after graduation.

Cohort milestones

  1. Month 0

    Align with HR and the sponsor

    Run a needs analysis, agree the target behaviour and success indicator, and ask the manager to record a baseline observation. Each participant completes one assessment, either DiSC or Strengthscope. Compare the two profiles.

  2. Self

    Lead yourself

    Use the assessment debrief to choose a personal habit to practise in a real work situation.

  3. People

    Lead through others

    Practise delegation, feedback and coaching. Bring an example from the workplace into the next session.

  4. Business

    Lead for the business

    Connect a team decision or improvement to an agreed business priority and review the evidence with the sponsor.

  5. +1 month

    Repeat the manager behaviour check

    Compare the same behaviour with the pre-programme observation. Record an example, the progress seen and the next action.

Leadership profiling

Choose a starting point for development.

Before the first module, each participant completes one online profile. Choose the assessment that best fits the cohort’s development goal.

Strengthscope®

What gives this leader energy?

Explore strengths across four areas: emotional, relational, thinking and execution. The individual report and debrief help the leader choose a strength to use more deliberately.

At work Choose a strength to draw on in a coaching conversation or an optional capstone project.

DiSC®

How does this leader work with others?

Explore how communication preferences, pace and responses to conflict shape everyday interactions. In Team Synergy, a team map helps colleagues compare their approaches.

At work Adapt a feedback conversation or delegation brief to the person receiving it.

  1. Before Module 1Complete the profile online.
  2. Practitioner debriefInterpret the profile and choose a development goal.
  3. During the programmePractise the behaviour with colleagues.
  4. At capstone, if selectedReview the goal against evidence from work.

Client experience

Leadership on the front line

Explore how OneSubsea, Insulet and SCHOTT Glass shaped leadership development around their teams.

Operations and quality assurance

OneSubsea’s cohort brings together supervisors working in operations and quality assurance. Their leadership responsibilities span operational delivery and quality oversight.

View OneSubsea’s programme plan

Effective Supervisory Development

Month 0
Orientation, manager evaluation, DiSC profile and individual feedback.
Months 1–3
Effective leadership, then assertive communication and feedback.
Months 4–7
Performance appraisal and motivation, followed by coaching skills. Managers check in at the midpoint.
Months 8–11
Time management and productivity, then creative problem-solving and decision-making.
Month 12
Business case presentation, graduation, final evaluation and report.

The outline pairs six two-day modules with five coaching sessions between workshops.

Proactive problem-solving

Insulet’s supervisors are developing how they address problems proactively and communicate with managers. These priorities give the cohort a practical focus for workplace conversations.

View Insulet’s programme plan

IMY Supervisory Academy

September
Orientation and DiSC debrief, followed by business English and reporting for supervisors.
October
Influencing without authority.
November
Managing time and stress with emotional intelligence, then resolving conflict through problem-solving and decision-making.
December
Dynamic supervisory skills, including delegation, coaching and follow-up.

The proposed capstone asks each supervisor to apply the five modules to one workplace challenge and present the evidence to management. Showcase timing is pending confirmation.

Developing future leaders

SCHOTT Glass brought self, team, organisational and operational leadership into one programme. Its plan paired DiSC profiling and 360° feedback with coaching, workplace application and a closing presentation to management.

Sample coaching report

What a manager can follow up

A short, participant-approved record gives the reporting manager one behaviour to observe and a date to review it.

Fictional coaching example · Shift handover

Who owns the next decision?

  1. Observed in role-play

    The supervisor asked for a recommendation but needed a prompt to agree when the team member should escalate.

  2. Next two handovers

    The supervisor will ask the team member to name the decision owner, the limit of their authority and a review time.

  3. Manager follow-up

    Observe one handover and record which of the three points were agreed. At the one-month check-in, compare it with the baseline.

View the full coaching action record

Coaching action record

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE
Workplace challenge
A shift supervisor takes back routine decisions when a handover is under pressure.
Coaching observation
In role-play, the supervisor asked the team member to recommend a next step. A prompt was needed to agree when to escalate.
Participant commitment
At the next two handovers, ask the team member to name an owner, a decision boundary and a review time.
Manager follow-up
Observe one handover and record whether all three points were agreed. Discuss what the supervisor could repeat or adjust.
Review date
At the agreed check-in one month after the programme, compare examples with the manager’s pre-programme behaviour check.

Coaching is a paid option. Agree with the participant which actions may be shared with their manager. Private session notes stay separate.
